instruction: In the calendar spreadsheet, find the first Saturday and first Sunday of each month (Jun through Oct) and set their cell background to red (#ff0000).

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to highlight all weekend dates across 5 months but failed. It correctly identified June 4-5 as Saturday-Sunday and selected B6:B7, applied partial red background. Then tried using Name Box with comma-separated multi-range but got a syntax error. Only managed to partially color a few cells.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open LibreOffice Calc, navigate cells, select cell ranges, apply background colors via highlighting button, use Name Box for cell selection
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because: (1) incorrectly mapped date-to-row for months other than June, (2) used commas instead of semicolons for Name Box multi-range selection, (3) ran out of turns after error recovery attempts.
metadata.task_rationale: Reduced from all weekends (~44 cells) to just the first weekend of each month (10 cells across 5 columns). Tests the model's ability to identify weekend dates and apply formatting across multiple columns but with much smaller scope.
metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the first Sat+Sun per month: Jun 4-5 (B6:B7), Jul 2-3 (C4:C5), Aug 6-7 (D8:D9), Sep 3-4 (E5:E6), Oct 1-2 (F3:F4). Getter reads fill colors. Metric checks each cell for FF0000 with partial credit (0.1 per cell).

scoring_breakdown.each_cell: 0.1 per correctly colored cell (10 cells total)

llm_judge_reasons: Cell references are correct for the calendar layout: Jun 4-5 (B6:B7), Jul 2-3 (C4:C5), Aug 6-7 (D8:D9), Sep 3-4 (E5:E6), Oct 1-2 (F3:F4) — verified against 2022 calendar where Jun 1=Wed, Jul 1=Fri, Aug 1=Mon, Sep 1=Thu, Oct 1=Sat
Getter correctly extracts cell fill colors via openpyxl with proper fallback logic (fgColor.rgb → start_color.rgb for solid fills), filtering out default '00000000' no-fill
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_color') and expected.get('cells') without incorrect nesting
Substring match ('FF0000' in actual.upper()) correctly handles ARGB format differences (e.g., 'FFFF0000' contains 'FF0000')
Complete coverage: all 10 cells (first Sat+Sun × 5 months Jun-Oct) are verified
Postconfig properly saves file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads from disk, ensuring fresh state
Partial credit scoring (0.1 per cell) is reasonable for a 10-cell task
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter's fill color detection could be more robust for edge cases with theme-based colors in openpyxl, but this is unlikely to affect cells explicitly set to #ff0000
